title: Fake campus drive with per-student registration payment vs. placement cell announcing a genuine drive
summary: A caller who says they are from the training and placement cell of Nilgiri Crest Institute of Technology phones a final-year student about a Vistara Infotech campus drive. In the fraud case, the caller asks each student to pay a "drive registration" amount to a UPI ID to receive the test link and admit card. In the legitimate case, the placement coordinator tells the student to register on the college placement portal, states the eligibility criteria, and says there is no charge.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a final-year B.Tech / BCA / MCA student at the college; branch and CGPA sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: graduate engineer trainee, CTC [AMOUNT_1] (₹3,50,000–₹5,50,000 per year).
Both calls mention the drive date, eligibility, the online aptitude test, and the words "registration" and "last date".

fraud.label_rationale: The caller requires the student to pay to register for a recruitment drive, to a personal UPI handle outside the college's own systems.
fraud.caller_objective: Collect small payments from many students; there is no drive.
stable_facts: Amount: [AMOUNT_2] (₹500–₹2,500), called "drive registration and test platform charge".
Paid to [UPI_ID_1]; the caller says the admit card and test link come by SMS after payment.
Caller says registration closes tonight and "only paid students will be allowed in the test".
Registration link is on a non-college domain: https://vistara-campusdrive.invalid.

cooperative.fraud: Agrees to pay and asks whether classmates should pay the same UPI ID
cooperative.legitimate: Says they will register tonight and asks about the test pattern

clarifying.fraud: Asks why this drive is not on the placement portal
clarifying.legitimate: Asks whether students with one backlog can apply

resistant.fraud: Says they will ask the placement officer in person tomorrow
resistant.legitimate: Says they are preparing for higher studies and may skip the drive

suspicious.fraud: Asks why the college would collect money through a personal UPI
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they know this call is really from the placement cell

fraud: caller says the portal is "down" and student still declines
legitimate: caller tells a suspicious student to check the notice on the portal or visit the placement office.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may lower the amount, claim a "group discount", or press the deadline. They must not switch to OTPs, remote access, or bank logins. The legitimate caller must not introduce any charge after the branch.

must_preserve: drive date, role, CTC, and eligibility identical across cases
_L college-portal registration with explicit no-charge statement

ambiguities: Some colleges charge a placement or training fee as part of official semester fees, receipted by the college. That is not modelled; _L states no charge for this drive.

Close to jr_01 in mechanism (pay to enter a selection process). The difference is the impersonated institution (the student's own college) and the collective, low-amount pattern. Flagged for deduplication review.
A caller knowing the student's name and branch is not evidence; both callers know it.

evidence_references.claim: Fake offers are followed by registration forms/admit cards and arrive through unsolicited messages (CJ03)
A major IT employer never asks candidates for payment at any stage (CJ01)
Upfront payment is a red flag in fake job schemes (C11)
